Bulk matrix initialization review (read-only)
Worktree /home/wishapig/hackathon-overnight/bulk-init, base9d542e621e80727a516d09c223b00030f7747222. Reviewed core.hpp/main.cpp/runtime.cpp diff89 additions/19 deletions. Requirements reread before review. No edits, compilation, numerical execution or profiler launched by this reviewer. Owner's existing Release main.o and runtime.o inspected read-only after owner build succeeded.

Result: no concrete blocking initialization, prefault-timing, synchronization, drain or resource-accounting defect found in current application call paths. No per-task scheduler overhead introduced: the branch is once per worker epoch, not in work(id)'s task loop. Functional/sanitizer/performance acceptance remains owner/root work.

Deferred allocation and current matrix paths (main.cpp30-39,630-649):
- Matrix custom allocator's zero-argument placement construct uses default initialization, starting double lifetime without writing its value. Nonzero-argument construct preserves forwarding, so range-copy trim does not discard input. The container remains contiguous and uses the same size/capacity semantics.
- Before resizing, old_a_size=min(a.size,e), old_l_size=min(l.size,e). Fresh allocation/growth beyond capacity first releases both old matrices (553-558), so new storage always has old_size0. Each newly created A logical element [old_a_size,e) is explicitly set0 before read(input). Old prefix is already touched from prior initialization/input; shrunk tail is either not used or zeroed when later reconstructed. No uninitialized A reaches finite check or I/O.
- For first unconditional Copy, L new logical tail is explicitly zeroed, preserving prior vector value-initialization; old prefix may retain values until Copy overwrites it. Without unconditional first Copy, including empty program/If-first, zero_l_from0 causes full logical L clearing every case. No stale previous output exposed.
- Executor exists only if a previous case created it and it survived budget checks. New bulk operation does not construct a pool. Without executor, ordinary std::fill_n runs serially. Explicit serial-stream still discards spare cache before allocation as in basebuffer candidate.
- Reclaim path resets/destroys executor first, frees L, copies complete current input with Matrix(a.begin,a.end), resizes newL, then explicitly std::fill(l.begin,l.end,0). This closes the otherwise dangerous default-initialization gap. A copy construction writes every value normally and is timed. No retry can occur after numerical_started.
- Final A/L Matrix swaps still precede score capture; deallocation remains timed.

Compiled prefault timing evidence (existing /tmp/night-bulk-build/CMakeFiles/dag_run.dir/src/main.cpp.o):
- main calls Executor::zero_ranges at relative offset3074 (relocation3075), returns and joins the input-read setup at3089/3091, then calls the existing read helper at30a1 (relocation30a2 -> .text+0x73c, helper begins740).
- no-executor branch has explicit memset calls at3818 and3847 (relocations3819 and3848); it then jumps back3091 before the same30a1 read helper. The initial A fill has not been optimized away.
- read helper itself starts the excluded I/O timer before std::istream::read, so all retained memset or zero_ranges rendezvous work is outside that exclusion and after case_start. Current compiled evidence supports R21. This does not guarantee future compilers behave identically; existing submission timing validation remains applicable.

Worker epoch happens-before proof (runtime.cpp445-513):
- zero_ranges obtains run_mutex, shared with run, set_budget and reservation. It cannot overlap a numerical run or another zero call through the public executor API. Caller writes both ZeroRange records before locking control, sets zero_job/active/epoch while holding control, then releases control through wait. Workers acquire control as their start_cv wait completes; range/job writes therefore happen-before their reads after unlock.
- Each worker computes a static disjoint range: width=count/workers, extra=count%workers, begin=width*id+min(id,extra), own count=width+(id<extra). These intervals exactly cover the supplied span without overlap; zero-sized spans never perform pointer arithmetic or stores in worker. The two actual caller spans are distinct A/L allocations. Partition boundaries may share a page/cacheline but not a double; that is performance-only.
- Workers finish zeroing, reacquire control, decrement active. Main waits under control until active0; completion of all stores happens-before return. It resets zero_job under control and clears ranges only after all workers have finished reading them. Workers loop back waiting on the unchanged epoch. Next numerical run publishes a new epoch with zero_jobfalse; no stale zero range is used.
- error is reset before publication. Existing fail records errors under error_mutex, then worker decrements active under control. Main only reads/rethrows after active0/acquire, so all workers are drained before an exception escapes. It clears zero_job/ranges even in that error path. Scalar fill_n cannot normally throw, but the lifecycle is still safe for recorded worker exceptions.
- Shutdown remains stop flag under control plus notify/join. Actual main resets executor only after synchronous zero_ranges/run returns, so no matrix lifetime race. No new worker threads, graph tasks, dependency edges, queues or per-task counters for bulk work.

Budget/semantics:
- Two pointer/count fields and a mode bool add bounded Impl state; no matrix scratch allocation or queue/graph storage occurs. Existing per-worker4096 bookkeeping allowance covers this small state. Actual A/L capacities continue in case matrix budget; runtime graph/execution reservations unchanged.
- Bulk is invoked only after prior case run drains. It cannot pipeline cases or prepare next input concurrently. Pool affinity/NUMA binding unchanged, therefore writes use the same allowed single-NUMA workers.
- Page/workers threshold chooses serial versus existing pool rendezvous from actual worker count and sysconf page size; it does not cap legal shapes. Application guards n*n<=INT_MAX, so first_count+second_count and bytes remain within64-bit arithmetic for actual callers. No new overflow audit is necessary in the task path.
- Existing exception boundaries preserved: a zeroing failure before input safely aborts; preparation reclaim still bounded; numerical task work is unchanged. Metadata unchanged and no audit/name/hash additions.

Potential performance limits, not correctness findings:
- sysconf plus run_mutex/rendezvous cost is once per nonempty initialization call; page-per-worker threshold is a heuristic whose full-score effect must be measured.
- The first case has no pool, so it initializes serially. Large later growth can use the existing pool; no promise of parallel initialization for all cases.
- Page/cacheline sharing at contiguous partition boundaries and memory bandwidth contention could limit gains. No evidence here warrants changing partition heuristics before the parent's score.

Reviewer remains idle; owner is conducting authorized build/functional tests. This review requests no new checks, audit fields or permanent test suite.

main uses vector<double,DeferredZeroAllocator<double>>; no-arg construction begins scalar lifetime without a store; copy construction still constructs supplied value. After resize, A newly added logical tail ALWAYS explicitly zeroed before read(input) begins. L new tail always zeroed; if no unconditional first Copy, entire logical L zeroed. No omission of previous zero semantics. One bulk rendezvous covers both spans; no existing executor means serial fill_n and no pool creation. All allocator/zero/wake/drain costs remain inside timed case before exempt I/O. A first pages cannot migrate into I/O exemption.

Capacity retention/budgets from buffer candidate unchanged: grow frees pair first; actual capacity charged; early cache reclaim probes again; one pre-numerical prepare retry only. Retry resets pool first, preserves A through value copy, new L explicitly serial fill0. All default-init construction call sites enumerated; no uninitialized data passed to numerical operations. No-copy/If/emptyProgram must use zero_l_from0; Copy prefix requires only newly created tail because old prefix was already initialized.

Boundaries/risks: parallel page faults may serialize in OS; memory-bandwidth saturation and waking many workers can outweigh gains. Uniform span partitions may share a boundary page/cache line but not elements; correctness unaffected, no page-layout change. No promise of proportional24x/64x gain. Existing pool only means first case and fresh process with no pool have no win. Matrix memory may be unchanged but timing of faults differs; this candidate requires complete score A/B and same public/resource/functional gates. If it loses, drop allocator and runtime bulk API together.
